target.title: NeuroTTT: Bridging Pretrain–Downstream Task Misalignment in EEG Foundation Models via Test-Time Training
target.venue: arXiv preprint (cs.LG; no journal or conference venue stated)

read.pdf: Tables 1–7 read from text.txt; figure captions and extracted text from Figures 1–3 read, figures not visually inspected (PDF not supplied)

target.first_public_note: arXiv identifier 2509.26301 (v1 September 2025); read as v2

entries.text: NeuroTTT aligns EEG foundation representations through domain-specific self-supervision and then test-time adaptation.
entries.condition: Two-stage approach; Stage I supervised task loss plus domain-specific SSL, Stage II SSL TTT or entropy minimization at inference.
entries.quote: In summary, we propose a novel two-stage alignment approach for EEG foundation models, our main contributions can be summarized as follows:

entries.text: Authors claim, to their knowledge, the first unification of domain-tuned self-supervision and test-time training for large EEG foundation models.
entries.condition: Novelty claim, qualified by authors' knowledge.

entries.text: Domain-specific SSL objectives use unlabeled EEG structure and are presented as requiring no additional labeled data.
entries.condition: Stopped-band prediction plus a task-specific transformation objective; losses jointly trained with the supervised task loss.
entries.quote: Crucially, these SSL tasks are plug-and-play and do not require additional labeled data

entries.text: SSL TTT adapts on each unlabeled test sample before prediction; the paper allows resetting after each sample or carrying state forward online.
entries.condition: One gradient step is described; no main-task label is used for test-time SSL adaptation.

entries.text: Tent minimizes prediction entropy and updates only batch-normalization affine parameters, optionally including running mean and variance.
entries.condition: Paper describes batch-level test adaptation; non-normalization weights are held fixed.

entries.text: Authors claim state-of-the-art performance across three tasks and superiority to conventional fine-tuning and adaptation methods.
entries.condition: Imagined speech, mental stress detection, and motor imagery; CBraMod and LaBraM backbones.

entries.text: Authors say Tent can outperform full-parameter SSL TTT in some cases, especially cross-subject transfer, and hypothesize that its restricted updates are more stable.
entries.condition: Qualified claim; not asserted for every metric or dataset.

entries.text: Authors state that LoRA has the worst performance among the compared strategies.
entries.condition: General statement in Results; table rankings vary by metric and task.

entries.text: Ablation text says TTT gains are modest on within-subject BCIC but substantial on the two cross-subject tasks.
entries.condition: Qualitative description of Figure 3 ablation; extracted figure values are unreadable in text.txt.
entries.quote: TTT delivers modest improvements on the BCIC dataset (within-subject, non–cross-subject), but yields substantial benefits on the two cross-subject tasks

entries.text: The three domain-specific SSL pairings are stopped-band prediction plus amplitude scaling for imagined speech, A–P flip for stress, and temporal jigsaw for motor imagery.
entries.condition: Each pair is used with the supervised downstream objective in Stage I; stopped-band frequency divisions differ by task.
entries.quote: The second task is also specifically tailored to each domain.

entries.text: CBraMod is described as pretrained on 12 public EEG datasets using masked patch reconstruction.
entries.condition: Foundation-model pretraining description; official pretrained weights used.

entries.text: LaBraM is described as pretrained on over 2,500 hours of EEG from around 20 datasets using masked neural-code prediction.
entries.condition: Foundation-model pretraining description; official pretrained weights used.

entries.text: The paper says all datasets are rereferenced, band-pass filtered following CBraMod, downsampled to 200 Hz, and segmented into 1-second windows; no task-specific feature engineering is applied.
entries.condition: Same stated preprocessing across adaptation methods; detailed reference and filter settings are deferred to CBraMod and not specified here.

entries.text: Training uses Adam and learning rate 1e-4; full-parameter fine-tuning includes LoRA layers or SSL heads.
entries.condition: Paper says training continues until validation performance converges; task-head size is 1–3 linear layers.

entries.text: Imagined-speech benchmark is BCIC2020-III, five imagined phrases/classes, 64 channels at 256 Hz; evaluation is within-subject on the competition-provided per-subject split and averaged across subjects.
entries.condition: Paper does not state the number of subjects or identify session-level partitions.
entries.quote: models are trained and tested on data from the same subject

entries.text: MentalArithmetic is binary stress detection using 20 channels recorded at 500 Hz; subjects 1–28 train, 29–32 validate, and 33–36 test under a held-out-subject protocol.
entries.condition: Test subjects are described as completely held out.
entries.quote: Subject 1 to 28 are set as training set, subject 29 to 32 are validation set and subiect 33 to 36 are set to test

entries.text: BCI Competition IV-2a is four-class MI with 22 channels at 250 Hz; subjects 1–5 train, 6–7 validate, and 8–9 test in the stated cross-subject split.
entries.condition: Predefined competition splits; paper does not identify sessions within each subject.
entries.quote: We follow the standard cross-subject evaluation: Subject 1-5, 6-7, 8-9 are used for training, validation, and test, respectively, the predefined splits from the competition.

entries.text: Authors report that cross-subject imagined-speech experiments were at chance for both backbones and therefore report within-subject results; no numeric chance score is given.
entries.condition: Cross-subject imagined speech; no numeric result, split, or chance benchmark reported.

entries.text: Table 7 reports one SSL TTT update per sample.
entries.condition: NeuroTTT (SSL) test-stage hyperparameter; see separate entries for remaining settings.
entries.quote: Steps 1

entries.text: Authors characterize Stage I as adding no deployment cost, while the separate test-time methods perform adaptation at inference.
entries.condition: No quantitative latency, memory, or device benchmark is reported.

entries.text: The paper describes test-time SSL adaptation as privacy-friendly because computation uses the test sample without sharing or storing source-domain data.
entries.condition: Author characterization; no deployment/privacy evaluation is reported.

entries.text: Authors concede that manually engineered SSL tasks encode priors that may not be universally optimal and may bias representations or yield negligible gains.
entries.condition: Automated SSL-task design or meta-selection is left for future work.

entries.text: Authors concede full-parameter SSL TTT may be unnecessary or unstable on noisy trials and propose restricted updates as future work.
entries.condition: Possible alternatives named are late blocks, normalization layers, or adapters.

entries.text: Authors concede TTT can perturb well-formed features on noisy or atypical trials; Tent may under-correct severe shifts because it updates normalization statistics only.
entries.condition: Stability-versus-adaptation-capacity trade-off.

entries.text: The repository fine-tuning script defaults to seed 3407, while the README quick-start example passes seed 8888; ttt_main.py has no seed argument. The paper does not identify which seed or repetitions generated Tables 1–3.
entries.unit: seed values in script default and README example
entries.condition: Repository code inspected at the current public main-branch snapshot; README calls its command a quick-start example, not the table-producing run.

entries.text: README's example speech config declares subject_range 1–16 and uses trial indices 300–349 for validation and 350–399 for test; it is explicitly an example, and the trial-based loader does not apply subject_range.
entries.condition: BCIC2020-3 sample configuration; all trials not selected by the test/validation predicates are assigned to training.

entries.text: The public speech, stress, and MI dataset loaders divide each stored EEG sample by 100 before tensor conversion; this amplitude scaling is not stated in the paper.
entries.condition: Applies in the three task dataset loaders; repository snapshot does not document the physical-unit rationale in those loaders.

entries.text: In the current repository, BCIC-IV-2a's validation DataLoader is constructed from test_set, not val_set; the trainer selects multiclass checkpoints using validation Cohen's kappa and then evaluates test data, so this loader causes test-subject data to serve validation as well.
entries.condition: Current public repository implementation; this conflicts with the paper's stated train/validation/test subject assignment and should not be assumed to be the exact run that produced the paper table.

entries.text: The public MI preprocessing code subtracts the instantaneous across-channel mean, applies a fifth-order 0.3–50 Hz Butterworth band-pass, retains 2–6 s after event onset, resamples each segment to 800 points, and then reshapes into four 200-point patches; these exact settings are absent from the paper.
entries.unit: filter order; Hz; seconds; samples; patches×samples
entries.condition: BCI IV-2a preprocessing script; dataset loader subsequently divides stored samples by 100 (t89).

entries.text: Current stress stopped-band code defines five frequency bins, including 30–45 Hz, whereas paper Table 5 lists four bins ending at 20–30 Hz.
entries.condition: Current repository implementation differs from the frequency-band table in the paper.

questions.q: What are the paper's primary quantitative results, and on what splits were they measured?
questions.answer: Tables 1–3 report the three metrics for six strategies and two backbones on within-subject five-class BCIC2020-III, held-out-subject binary MentalArithmetic, and cross-subject four-class BCI IV-2a. Each result entry preserves its dataset, subjects/split, method, backbone, units, and source row.

questions.q: What are the main methodological contribution and the authors' stated limitations?
questions.answer: The contribution is domain-specific SSL fine-tuning combined with unlabeled test-time SSL or entropy minimization. Authors claim novelty and state-of-the-art results, while conceding task-design dependence, possible instability of full-parameter TTT, and Tent's limited capacity for severe shifts.

questions.q: What evaluation details remain uncertain or require checking against the released code?
questions.answer: The paper leaves seeds/repetitions, the meaning of ±, chance scores, speech validation membership, session membership, preprocessing details, and pretraining-subject overlap unspecified. The current repository includes a sample speech split, scaling by 100, an MI validation loader wired to test data, and code-level differences in the stress band bins, Tent normalization updates, and TTT optimizer/settings.
